supporting_observations.claim: Two network logon attempts for max.fischer failed with an incorrect-password status, from 192.0.2.199, at 13:39:57 and 13:41:14 UTC.

At 13:42:26 UTC, a network logon for max.fischer succeeded from the same IP address and with the same process ID shown in the failed attempts; the successful event lists Kerberos, whereas the failures list Negotiate/NTLM.
The failures followed by a successful logon from the same IP are suspicious, but these records alone do not establish whether the source was authorized or who initiated the attempts.

known_telemetry_limitations: The authentication records identify the source as 192.0.2.199 but do not identify a source hostname or user operating it.
The records show a successful network logon but do not identify the resource accessed or establish what activity followed from that logon.
claims_not_established: Whether 192.0.2.199 corresponds to an authorized device or to an unauthorized actor.
Whether max.fischer initiated or authorized the failed and successful attempts.
Whether the successful network logon enabled access to any resource or involved malicious intent.
additional_evidence_needed: Resolve 192.0.2.199 to a device or network location using DHCP, network, firewall, and endpoint records for the time of the attempts.

Review domain-controller and resource-access telemetry around 13:39–13:43 UTC, including applicable logon, share-access, and authentication records, to determine what the successful network logon accessed.
Confirm with max.fischer whether the attempts and successful authentication were expected.
unrelated_findings: On WS-MFISCHER-01, max.fischer launched msi_update.exe from the user Temp directory after an interactive logon; it created a file in C:\Windows\Temp and then exited. This is a separate item to investigate and is not linked by these records to the alerted network logons. (T231-00005, T231-00010, T231-00014, T231-00016, T231-00017)
